text:
Alyssa: quick sync — Acme asked for per-request token breakdown + a per-response cost field. We need to nail scope and launch acceptance. thoughts?
Chen: keep it minimal. fields: trace_id, request_id (optional), tokens_input, tokens_output, cost_usd. Short names save tokens.
Ravi: naming affects downstream billing/joins. Can we namespace? e.g. token_usage_input / token_usage_output so it's obvious.
Maya: namespace increases char count but is clearer. downside: some SDKs map nested objects -> extra parsing. prefer flat keys to avoid surprises.
Chen: flat wins for perf. propose tokens_in / tokens_out, plus trace_id.
Alyssa: Acme needs to join LLM calls to their logs using their existing request id. They asked for a canonical field name we can guarantee. Do we standardize on trace_id and accept request_id as passthrough header?
Ravi: standardize on trace_id (128-bit hex). Accept request_id header forwarded into metadata but not required to be computed by us. We'll document aliasing.
Maya: function/tool calls are important for them as well. We should include function_call.name and function_call.called (bool) and function_call.args_truncated (bool). But nested function_call object adds bytes. Alternative: function_name, function_called, function_args_truncated.
Chen: agree: flatten: function_name, function_called, function_args_truncated. Keep types simple: string/bool.
Alyssa: also we have multi-mode API (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). We need a mode field so customers can interpret other fields (e.g., embedding_dim only present for embeddings).
Maya: propose 'mode' enum: chat|completion|embed|rerank.
Ravi: embeddings need embedding_dim and optional vector. For privacy we should keep vectors out of telemetry, but allow storing embedding_dim and vector_length.
Chen: minimal response envelope example (for docs/SDKs):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-v1",
  "mode": "chat",
  "trace_id": "f1e2d3c4a5b6...",
  "tokens_in": 42,
  "tokens_out": 128,
  "cost_usd": 0.0034,
  "function_name": "summarize_article",
  "function_called": true,
  "function_args_truncated": false
}
```
Maya: note: for embeddings we'd add: "embedding_dim": 1536, "vector_present": false (customers can opt-in to store).
Alyssa: Launch acceptance checklist (proposal):
- Docs: example payloads for chat/completion/embeddings/rerank (yes)
- Export: per-request token totals available in Console and API (yes)
- Canary: run with 3 pilot customers (incl. Acme) for 2 weeks; no more than 2 regressions per 10k requests
- Performance SLO: 95th latency < 200ms for short chat, 99th < 400ms when not batching; must be measurable in console
- Rollout plan & rollback knob in place
Ravi: callout — 99th 400ms will need Dedicated routing for strict cases. Ops needs to reserve capacity.
deploy-bot: Canary capacity reserved: 2x baseline in prod-us-west for window 2024-11-02T02:00:00Z -> 2024-11-16T02:00:00Z.
Maya: token cost impact study: I will run simulations on 3 representative prompts and report delta for different field name choices (tokens_in vs token_usage_input) — shorter key names should save ~1-3 tokens per call at scale.
Chen: action items: 1) I will open a schema PR with flat key names + example payloads (due: EOD Friday). 2) Maya will attach perf/token sims. 3) Ravi will draft canary runbook with acceptance metrics and rollback steps.
Alyssa: one more: please include a migration/compatibility plan. Some customers already parse existing metadata; we need to support a short deprecation window for aliases (e.g., accept request_id and requestId).
Ravi: agree — we should accept common aliases server-side and emit canonical names in responses. Make that explicit in the API changelog.
Chen: sending initial PR now. will include examples for function calling and embedding payloads.
Maya: will post perf numbers and a quick cost table in this thread when ready.
Alyssa: thanks all. if no objections by EOD Friday we lock schema and start docs + SDK updates. :thumbsup:
